What the app does
It is a local traffic filter for Mobile Legends. It does not speed up the internet and does not change the account region — it lets you “hide” battle servers with bad ping from the game so it picks good ones. Nothing is sent anywhere: only the game is intercepted, other apps work directly.

Quick start
1. On the Status tab tap Start and allow the VPN (other VPNs must be off — Android allows only one).
2. Open the game and play 1–3 matches. The Servers tab fills with servers, in-game ping, country and provider.
3. Tap the ping button (📶) to ping all servers — the list sorts best to worst. Servers are pinged one by one with pauses, so the mass ping does not skew the results.
4. Tap Only this on the best server (or “Keep only this one” on the Status tab). Done: the other game servers are blocked, new ones get blocked automatically.

Favorites tab
Your chosen servers with auto-ping (interval in Settings). ICMP ping is a proxy: the real ping in battle is the “in game” value measured from the game’s own probes. Some servers do not answer ICMP at all — then only the in-game ping is shown.

Server types
• MATCH — battle server. Ping in battle = ping to it.
• PROBE — candidates the game probes before matchmaking. The honest in-game ping is measured here.
• LOBBY — account, chat and matchmaking server. Do not block.
• OTHER — login, shop, updates, ads, analytics. Blocking is useless and harmful.

What “blocked” means
For the game the server looks dead: silence on UDP, refusal on TCP. If a battle is running on that server, the block is applied “after match” so you are not kicked.

If something goes wrong
• Matchmaking hangs / “reconnecting” — the favorite is overloaded or in maintenance. Tap Remove all blocks, play a match, pick a server again.
• The filter turns off by itself — disable battery optimization for the app (menu → Battery) and do not swipe the notification away.
• “VPN error” — turn off other VPNs/proxies and “Always-on VPN” in Android settings.

Ping colors: green — up to 60 ms, yellow — up to 120 ms, red — above. Tap a card to see ports, traffic and details.
